claim: The RxC (rows-by-columns) ecological inference case -- used by both PyEI's ei_rxc() and eiCompare's ei_rxc() for simultaneous multi-candidate/multi-group estimation -- traces to King, Rosen & Tanner (2001), 'Bayesian and Frequentist Inference for Ecological Inference: The RxC Case,' establishing the RxC model as an extension beyond King's original 1997 2x2 method.
stance_target: methodological lineage of the RxC ecological-inference estimator implemented in both PyEI and eiCompare
scope_conditions: statistical methodology literature, general applicability beyond the US racial-voting context
quoted_support: [Paper] Bayesian and Frequentist Inference for Ecological Inference: The RxC Case (2001)

claim: Ecological inference methodology has continued to develop after King's original 1997 solution, including a 2019 refinement ('Ecological Regression With Partial Identification') addressing partial (non-point) identification of aggregate-to-individual inference -- indicating the field treats EI as having inherent identification limits that later work tries to formally bound rather than eliminate.
stance_target: ecological inference remains a methodologically contested/evolving technique with acknowledged identification limits, relevant to assessing its reliability for bureau-de-vote-level projection
